attack_vector: A2 -- is Re Li2 continuous across the cut? YES

gates.claim: A2's premise: Li2's discontinuity across [1,inf) is EXACTLY 2*pi*i*log(x) -- purely imaginary. So Re Li2 is CONTINUOUS across the cut even though Li2 is not. The Re jump measures as zero; the Im jump is nonzero and matches the prediction, which is what makes the zero meaningful rather than a null result

the SAME for the full Rogers L, which is what is actually needed. Both of its terms jump -- Li2 by 2*pi*i*log x, and log(x)*log(1-x)/2 because log(1-x) crosses log's cut -- and BOTH jumps are purely imaginary, so Re L is continuous across [1,inf). Checking Li2 alone would not have settled this

THE REDUCTION. Given G1/G2, the inversion leg is equivalent to the REAL identity Re Li2(x) + Li2(1/x) = pi^2/3 - (1/2)log^2(x) for x > 1 -- in which 1/x lies in (0,1), where the series converges and cLiTwo_ofReal already bridges. No boundary value, no cut-crossing, no new analytic infrastructure. This is a different and much smaller problem than the one qou-invr recorded

WHICH SIDE Lean's own definition lands on, measured rather than reasoned. cLiTwoExt y = -int_0^1 log(1 - y t)/t dt with the principal branch, at real x > 1, equals Li2(x - i0) -- the LOWER boundary value. I PREDICTED THE UPPER ONE before measuring, from arg(negative real) = +pi, and was wrong. Recorded because branch signs are exactly what this lane has repeatedly got wrong. The conclusion does not depend on it: the REAL PART agrees with both sides

the target itself: extend(pi^2/6, rogersL)(x) = Re L(x) for x > 1, 200 points. And at w_1 = 1/(1-x_root) = 2.24698 -- the ONE argument of the six that `extended_sum` uses in this regime, and the whole of what qou-rstq item 4 still lacks

WHAT REMAINS, named so this probe is not misread as closing qou-invr. Two things, both smaller than a boundary-value theory but neither free: (1) INTEGRABILITY of the defining integral at x > 1 -- Lean's intervalIntegrable_log_one_sub_div_of_notCut assumes notCut, which FAILS here, so cLiTwoExt at x > 1 is currently a Lean `integral` with no proof its integrand is integrable, and an unproved-integrable integral is the junk value 0. The singularity at t = 1/x is logarithmic, hence integrable, but that needs proving. (2) the real identity of G3. Item 4 is NOT closed
still_needed: IntervalIntegrable (fun t => log(1 - x*t)/t) volume 0 1, for real x > 1
Re Li2(x) + Li2(1/x) = pi^2/3 - (1/2) log^2 x, for real x > 1
gates.no_longer_needed: a boundary value of Li2 obtained from off the cut; the real part is continuous across it (G1/G2), so there is nothing to take a limit of

verdict.measured: Li2's jump across [1,inf) is exactly 2*pi*i*log(x), purely imaginary, so Re Li2 -- and Re of the full Rogers L -- is CONTINUOUS across the cut. Lean's integral definition lands on the lower boundary value, but its real part agrees with both sides.
verdict.changes: the inversion leg is NOT a boundary-value problem. It reduces to one real identity, Re Li2(x) + Li2(1/x) = pi^2/3 - (1/2)log^2 x, whose partner argument 1/x lies safely in (0,1).
verdict.still_open: integrability of the defining integral at x > 1 (logarithmic singularity at t = 1/x -- integrable, but Lean's existing lemma assumes notCut and does not apply), and the real identity itself. qou-rstq item 4 remains open at exactly one argument, w_1 = 2.24698.
verdict.prediction_falsified: I expected the integral to pick the UPPER boundary value; it picks the lower. Immaterial to the conclusion, recorded anyway.
